description: A pure CALCULATION node — cyclically roll a matrix's ROWS. This is how you say "neighbour" for a vertex list: shift by -1 lines each vertex up with its NEXT one, by +1 with its PREVIOUS. Draws nothing.
instructions:
A value-only node: a matrix in, the same matrix with its rows rotated, out. It has no geometry input or output and draws nothing on the canvas.

WHY IT EXISTS: anything defined BETWEEN adjacent vertices — edge vectors, turn angles, curvature, corner bisectors — needs each row paired with its neighbour. Rolling the rows lets you express that with plain matrix arithmetic instead of a Loop.

INPUT: wire a matrix into valin-matrix — typically a POINT LIST (`val-points` from Polygon / Space Geometry / Vertices, an N×2 array of [x, y] metre pairs).

SHIFT BY: an integer, wrapping around the ends (the list is treated as a closed ring, which is what a polygon is).
• -1 → each row holds its NEXT neighbour. `Shift(P, -1) − P` via Matrix Operations (Subtract) is the EDGE-VECTOR list.
• +1 → each row holds its PREVIOUS neighbour (the edge arriving at that vertex).

OUTPUT: `val-matrix` (same shape as the input) plus `val-rows` / `val-cols`. Every parameter is wireable (valin-*).
